video_title: Why Architecture Decisions Disappear and How ADRs Fix It
core_insight: An ADR is a time-stamped audit trail of why an architecture choice was made under specific constraints, not documentation of what was built. It makes trade-offs explicit now so you can learn from them later.

scenes.voice: Six months after shipping, a new engineer asks: Why did we pick Kafka over SQS for events?
scenes.visual: Engineer at desk, Slack thread and old design doc on screen, question bubble 'Why Kafka?'
scenes.on_screen_text: Why did we pick Kafka over SQS?

scenes.voice: The answer is in a Slack thread, a lost doc, or someone's head. Teams re-debate the same choice, or undo it without knowing the constraints that shaped it.
scenes.visual: Split screen: fading Slack messages, unlinked doc, person leaving. Redo icon over architecture diagram.

scenes.voice: As systems grow, decisions compound. Requirements change, people leave, code drifts from intent. Without a durable record of why, you lose accountability and waste time reconstructing history.
scenes.visual: Timeline of system growth, people icons leaving, code diverging from intent arrow.

scenes.voice: An Architecture Decision Record is a lightweight, time-stamped log of a significant choice and the reasoning behind it. Think of it as a commit message for architecture.
scenes.visual: Markdown file /docs/adr/001-kafka-events.md opens. Fields appear: Context, Options, Decision, Consequences.

scenes.voice: Context and constraints at the time, options considered, decision made, consequences accepted. Status moves Proposed to Accepted to Superseded. You never edit an old ADR, you create a new one that links back.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    Context[Context + Constraints] --> Options[Options]
    Options --> Decision[Decision]
    Decision --> Consequences[Consequences]
    Consequences --> ADR[ADR Accepted]
    ADR -->|time passes| Review[Review / New Context]
    Review -->|changed| NewADR[New ADR Supersedes]

scenes.voice: This helps with memory loss for new hires, prevents re-debate by showing what was known then, and makes risk visible. Don't ADR every dependency bump. Use it when the choice shapes the system and is hard to reverse.
scenes.visual: Checklist appears: data model, service boundaries, consistency model, deployment topology. Threshold note: hard to reverse >1 sprint?

scenes.voice: Trade-off: ADRs can rot if never updated, or create noise if overused. Keep the template minimal, time-box to about twenty minutes, and treat the record as a hypothesis with metrics that would prove it wrong.
scenes.visual: Warning icons for ADR rot and over-documentation, then minimal template and metric gauge.

mental_model: Treat architecture as a series of time-bound hypotheses. An ADR captures the context, options, and accepted trade-offs at that moment, so future you can judge if the hypothesis still holds instead of re-debating from scratch.
final_takeaway: ADRs don't guarantee the right decision, they make the reasoning inspectable and reversible over time.
